headline: Inkwell AI tool turns messy notes into formatted PDFs
summary: This open-source AI tool uses Gemma models to automatically format raw lecture notes into clean PDFs with rendered math, saving students hours of manual work.
details: Inkwell is an open-source, AI-powered tool designed to transform messy, plain-text lecture notes into beautifully formatted PDFs. It uses Gemma open-weight models to distill chaotic class notes into elegant, readable study materials, automatically rendering mathematical formulas with KaTeX.

Built for students, researchers, and engineers, Inkwell addresses the time-consuming process of manually retyping notes into LaTeX or Notion. Users paste raw notes, pick a layout, and the AI handles the structure and formatting, including converting plain-text equations into KaTeX.

To ensure mathematical accuracy, Inkwell employs a 'math guard' system. It uses regex heuristics to find raw equations and swap them for placeholders before processing by the AI, then verifies that every placeholder survives and replaces it with the formatted KaTeX output.

The tool also features a drawing canvas overlay with pen, highlighter, and eraser tools, allowing users to sketch diagrams or annotate directly on the rendered math. This ensures that annotations are preserved in the final output.

Inkwell exports a true vector PDF, maintaining crisp math fonts and including all user annotations. The frontend serializes the live DOM, including rendered KaTeX, and sends it to the backend for PDF compilation using Playwright, avoiding potential issues with standard print functions.

The application is deployed on Render, making it accessible via a link without any installation required. This accessibility, combined with the use of open-weight models like Gemma, means Inkwell can be used without monthly subscriptions or complex setup.

Inkwell's open-source nature (MIT license) allows for customization. Users can modify LaTeX rules, add support for other subjects like chemistry, build custom themes, or self-host the application offline, offering flexibility and privacy by potentially running models locally.
